name: github.com/pmezard/go-difflib
remediation_notes: The maintainer abandoned this package a decade ago, but it's stable, small (891 LOC), and does one focused thing well. Dependents should pin the version; the risk is minimal for diff generation, a well-understood problem that won't break from bitrot.

name: github.com/davecgh/go-spew
remediation_notes: Small, stable debugging utility with zero external dependencies. Hasn't needed changes in 8 years. Most dependents should pin the version. Projects seeking to eliminate the dependency can inline the 4,259-line codebase.

name: gopkg.in/check.v1
remediation_notes: 273K dependent repos spread across the Go ecosystem with no obvious steward. Testify is the de facto Go standard and actively maintained; migrate assertions and basic suite patterns there. Projects with advanced suite features may need ginkgo or deeper refactoring.

name: gopkg.in/yaml.v2
remediation_notes: Unmaintained since ~2020. Migrate to yaml.v3, the actively maintained successor with compatible API for most code.

name: github.com/golang/protobuf
remediation_notes: Switch to google.golang.org/protobuf, Google's official maintained successor. v1.4+ already delegates to it, making the migration straightforward with full feature parity.

name: golang.org/x/xerrors
remediation_notes: This forward-compatibility layer was superseded by Go 1.13's error wrapping (fmt.Errorf %w verb) and Go 1.20's errors.Join. Migrate to standard library error handling.

name: github.com/google/go-cmp
remediation_notes: Google maintains go-cmp passively as a stable utility—recent commits confirm ongoing care despite infrequent releases. No alternative offers equivalent comparison semantics. Pin the version and continue using it.

name: github.com/kr/text
remediation_notes: Stable text-formatting library unmaintained for 6+ years but free of known flaws or broken transitive dependencies. Downstream packages can safely continue using it by pinning to a known version.

name: github.com/pkg/errors
remediation_notes: Go 1.13+ stdlib provides native error wrapping (fmt.Errorf("%w", ...), errors.Is/As). Migrate to stdlib error handling; pkg/errors was a precursor now superseded.

name: github.com/kr/pty
remediation_notes: The original maintainer officially migrated this package to github.com/creack/pty, which is actively maintained. Update imports to the new module path.

name: github.com/kr/pretty
remediation_notes: kr/pretty has been unmaintained for 1338 days with no recent activity, but serves 195k+ dependent repos. Switch to davecgh/go-spew, the standard maintained alternative for pretty-printing Go values.

name: golang.org/x/lint
remediation_notes: golang.org/x/lint was deprecated by the Go team in favor of golangci-lint, which is actively maintained and widely used across the Go ecosystem. Use golangci-lint as a drop-in replacement for linting.

name: github.com/golang/mock
remediation_notes: gomock is archived and unmaintained since June 2023. The project explicitly recommends switching to go.uber.org/mock, an actively maintained fork that is a drop-in replacement for mockgen.

name: github.com/client9/misspell
remediation_notes: k8s.io/test-infra accounts for ~80% of usage and has capacity to maintain a fork. With zero dependencies and stable, mature functionality, coordination among major dependents is viable.

name: github.com/rogpeppe/go-internal
remediation_notes: Stable testing utilities maintained by Go contributors. Last release was 427 days ago but the repo receives reactive commits; accept as a pinned long-term dependency.

name: github.com/kisielk/gotool
remediation_notes: 90% of usage flows through gogo/protobuf; the 809-line utility library has zero dependencies and hasn't needed changes in eight years, making it trivial to inline. The dominant dependent could absorb it cleanly rather than keep the unmaintained package in scope.

name: github.com/json-iterator/go
remediation_notes: json-iterator/go is archived. Switch to Go's standard library encoding/json, which is the maintained drop-in replacement this library was designed to optimize. The stdlib has steadily improved in performance.

name: github.com/modern-go/concurrent
remediation_notes: Map backport is obsolete (sync.Map in stdlib since Go 1.9); Executor is a simple pattern easily inlined or replaced with stdlib context + goroutines or golang.org/x/sync primitives.

name: github.com/modern-go/reflect2
remediation_notes: Pin the version—the library is stable but unmaintained. Accept it for performance-critical reflection code; projects using it only transitively should consider switching to the standard library's reflect package instead.

name: github.com/google/uuid
remediation_notes: Dormancy is expected—RFC 9562 is stable and UUID generation is a solved algorithm with no dependencies. Pin the version and monitor Go compatibility changes, but no action required for most users.

name: github.com/mattn/go-colorable
remediation_notes: Stable Windows terminal colors utility with 134k dependent repos but no dead transitive dependencies. Last commit 473 days ago reflects code completion, not abandonment. No maintained drop-in replacement exists.

name: github.com/google/gofuzz
remediation_notes: Google archived this testing utility because property-based fuzzing has no active development cycle. The code is stable and self-contained with no transitive dependencies. Pin versions and accept the archive status rather than fork it.

name: github.com/konsorten/go-windows-terminal-sequences
remediation_notes: This 100-line wrapper for Windows terminal colors is stable but unmaintained. Projects should vendor the minimal code they need rather than maintain a live dependency.

name: github.com/google/btree
remediation_notes: Stable algorithmic library with no external dependencies; archived after maturity, not due to defects. Safe to pin and continue using.

name: github.com/hashicorp/golang-lru
remediation_notes: Dormant but stable LRU cache with 128k distributed dependents. No maintained replacement available; pin the version and accept the risk.

name: github.com/census-instrumentation/opencensus-proto
remediation_notes: Archived by design as part of the OpenCensus/OpenTracing merger into OpenTelemetry (sunsetting announced July 2023). Pin this version as a stable base while planning migration via language-specific OpenTelemetry bridges.

name: github.com/gogo/protobuf
remediation_notes: Switch to google.golang.org/protobuf, actively maintained by Google. It superseded gogo by adding the convenience methods that made gogo popular. Regenerate protos with the new plugin; migration is standard.

name: github.com/golang/groupcache
remediation_notes: groupcache is mature, stable code that doesn't require active development. Its distributed in-process caching design has no drop-in replacement, and it's too widely depended on to fork. Pin the version and carry the risk forward.

name: github.com/mitchellh/mapstructure
remediation_notes: Stable library after 4+ years completing its design. With 32k package dependents, forking is impractical. Pin the version and accept the low risk of an unmaintained utility, or vendor into critical infrastructure if needed.

name: go.uber.org/atomic
remediation_notes: Stable Uber library providing typed wrappers for atomic operations. Go 1.19+ includes equivalent generics in stdlib; plan to switch when upgrading Go versions. Until then, this is safe to pin—no active maintenance is needed.

name: github.com/ghodss/yaml
remediation_notes: Unmaintained but stable wrapper around go-yaml. Pin the version and keep go-yaml updated. No drop-in replacement; switching requires code changes and isn't practical for 120k+ dependents.

name: github.com/go-stack/stack
remediation_notes: Stable stack-tracing utility with a cleaner API than runtime.Callers; feature-complete with zero dependencies. Dormancy poses no risk—pin and rely on it.

name: github.com/google/renameio
remediation_notes: Atomic file operations are core to staticcheck's test infrastructure. The code is simple and unlikely to need changes; adoption is straightforward ownership transfer. For the tiny tail of direct dependents, vendoring is viable if adoption doesn't happen.

name: github.com/google/martian
remediation_notes: Stable testing proxy with zero runtime dependencies; safe to pin if you use it for testing. Large dependents like cloud.google.com/go should consider forking if future Go compatibility becomes critical.

name: github.com/creack/pty
remediation_notes: Stable Unix PTY library with concentrated usage through maintained intermediaries (kr/pty, survey, Netflix/go-expect, AWS agent). Zero runtime dependencies means no supply chain decay; pin the version and monitor the few-large dependents.

name: github.com/jstemmer/go-junit-report
remediation_notes: Stable tool that's complete and working. Input and output formats (Go test, JUnit XML) are stable; maintenance isn't needed. Most of the 111K repos depend through major Google projects like OpenCensus. Pin the version and accept the minimal risk of keeping unmaintained, proven code.

name: github.com/BurntSushi/xgb
remediation_notes: Original maintainer explicitly recommends switching to the jezek/xgb fork, which serves as the active maintenance point. Most usage flows through golang.org/x/exp; smaller GUI tool dependents should follow the same migration.

name: github.com/gorilla/websocket
remediation_notes: Gorilla WebSocket is stable and widely used but dormant with no maintenance activity for over a year. nhooyr.io/websocket is an actively maintained alternative with compatible APIs and better long-term support.

name: github.com/inconshreveable/mousetrap
remediation_notes: Windows-only, single-function library with stable 37-line implementation and no dependencies. Dependents should vendor the code directly and drop the dependency rather than maintain a reference to an unresponsive package.

name: github.com/beorn7/perks
remediation_notes: Algorithm is stable and proven. Pin versions, or vendor the 3K LOC if you need to modify it.

name: github.com/matttproud/golang_protobuf_extensions
remediation_notes: Explicitly retiring but stable for 7+ years. This is a small (816 LOC), complete utility for length-delimited protobuf messages. No maintenance needed; safe to pin the version and use indefinitely.

name: github.com/mitchellh/go-homedir
remediation_notes: At 256 lines with no dependencies, copy this into your codebase. For Go 1.12+, os.UserHomeDir() handles the main use case if you don't need path expansion.

name: github.com/rogpeppe/fastuuid
remediation_notes: 6+ years unmaintained but stable. Most dependents can switch to google/uuid (Google's maintained standard). Fastuuid trades randomness for speed—projects needing predictability could fork the small codebase.

name: github.com/julienschmidt/httprouter
remediation_notes: Stable but unmaintained; Go's stdlib mux (1.22+) and Chi both offer drop-in replacements. Chi maintains API compatibility if pattern syntax is the blocker for stdlib migration.

name: github.com/alecthomas/template
remediation_notes: This fork of Go 1.4's text/template is unmaintained and frozen in time. Most dependents should migrate to Go's modern stdlib text/template; projects specifically using the newline elision feature should implement it separately or maintain their own fork.

name: dmitri.shuralyov.com/gpu/mtl
remediation_notes: Metal GPU binding library with 99.7% usage concentrated through golang.org/x/exp. No maintained alternative exists; dependents should pin the version and accept the unmaintained status.

name: github.com/cncf/udpa/go
remediation_notes: Package archived and moved to github.com/cncf/xds for active development of xDS APIs. Dependents should migrate to the xDS replacement.

name: github.com/kr/logfmt
remediation_notes: kr/logfmt hasn't been maintained for 5+ years; switch to go-logfmt/logfmt, which is actively maintained and a drop-in replacement for logfmt parsing.

name: github.com/russross/blackfriday/v2
remediation_notes: Blackfriday v2 has been inactive since 2021 and explicitly deprecated. Migrate to goldmark for the vast majority of use cases; projects relying on specific features like Smartypants rendering may need to combine it with additional packages.

name: github.com/go-kit/kit
remediation_notes: Large toolkit spanning logging, metrics, tracing, service discovery, and more. Dependents should migrate by replacing each used component with specialized alternatives rather than seeking a single replacement.

name: github.com/cpuguy83/go-md2man/v2
remediation_notes: Dormant but stable CLI for a specific task (markdown to man pages); 100k+ dependents with no clear steward or maintained alternative. Safe to pin—the code is small and the man page format won't break.

name: gopkg.in/tomb.v1
remediation_notes: Unmaintained for 11 years but only 195 lines of code. Copy it into your project to eliminate the dependency.

name: github.com/dgrijalva/jwt-go
remediation_notes: The original maintainer archived this repo and officially migrated users to golang-jwt/jwt. It's a maintained fork and drop-in replacement.

name: github.com/mwitkow/go-conntrack
remediation_notes: Dormant 6+ years but stable with no external dependencies. Either pin the version and accept the risk (recommended for most), or vendor the 810 LOC if you want to eliminate the external dep.

name: github.com/magiconair/properties
remediation_notes: Dormant but stable with zero transitive issues. Pinning the version across 98k dependents costs less than coordinated migration.

name: github.com/gorilla/mux
remediation_notes: Pin the version and audit which features you actually use—basic routing can move to Go's stdlib (1.22+), advanced routing to chi or gin. Full migration across 97k repos isn't practical.

name: github.com/spf13/jwalterweatherman
remediation_notes: Unmaintained since 2018 but stable. Dependents should pin the version; new projects should use Go 1.21+ log/slog instead.

name: github.com/golang/snappy
remediation_notes: Snappy is stable infrastructure code archived by design; pin the version and monitor for CVEs. The Go implementation is the format reference and fills a unique speed/ratio niche—fork or vendor only if a security issue emerges.

name: github.com/hpcloud/tail
remediation_notes: nxadm/tail is the maintained successor fork with compatible APIs. Verify it covers your use cases before migrating; each dependent project needs to update their imports independently.

name: github.com/chzyer/readline
remediation_notes: Readline is stable but dormant (no commits in 312 days). The 96k dependents use different feature subsets; projects should migrate to golang.org/x/term for basics, bubbletea for modern interfaces, or fork if deep readline features are essential.

name: github.com/chzyer/test
remediation_notes: 93.9% of usage concentrates in chzyer/readline, an unmaintained sibling. At 561 LOC, the library is small enough to copy into readline or other dependents, eliminating the unmaintained dependency.

name: github.com/chzyer/logex
remediation_notes: logex is stable but unmaintained. Switch to logrus or log/slog (Go 1.21+) for ongoing support and security updates; similar API surface but requires some code changes.

name: github.com/coreos/go-semver
remediation_notes: Small, stable semver parsing library with 95K+ dependents. Alternatives exist but coordinating ecosystem-wide migration is impractical. Pin the version and keep watching; the compact codebase can be forked if needed.

name: github.com/shurcooL/sanitized_anchor_name
remediation_notes: Copy the 37-line function into your codebase. It has no dependencies and is stable; the code is simpler to maintain inline than as an external dependency.

name: github.com/cespare/xxhash/v2
remediation_notes: This is a mature hash function that's intentionally stable. The 754 days without commits reflects completeness, not abandonment. Pin the version and monitor for security advisories, but the low-risk profile suits indefinite maintenance as-is.

name: github.com/spaolacci/murmur3
remediation_notes: Stable hash algorithm unchanged in 8+ years. Projects can confidently pin this version. Switching requires adopting a different hash function (xxhash, crypto/blake2, etc.).

name: github.com/hashicorp/go-multierror
remediation_notes: Go 1.20+ stdlib's errors.Join() replaces basic aggregation; package readme recommends the switch. Use errgroup for concurrent collection. Pin the version for projects needing Group, Flatten, or Prefix.

name: github.com/hashicorp/errwrap
remediation_notes: Go 1.13+ provides built-in error wrapping via fmt.Errorf("%w", err), errors.Is(), and errors.As(). Dependents should migrate to stdlib error handling instead of maintaining this external dependency.

name: github.com/OneOfOne/xxhash
remediation_notes: Last commit in 2022 with no maintenance activity; the README recommends cespare/xxhash as a comparable actively maintained alternative. Dependents should switch rather than fork or vendor this stable, focused library.

name: github.com/cespare/xxhash
remediation_notes: xxhash is stable and implementation-complete. With 84k dependents and no viable alternative, ecosystem migration creates more disruption than benefit. Accept and pin the version.

name: github.com/smartystreets/assertions
remediation_notes: Dormant but stable assertion library used across 84k repos with no practical migration path; pin to a known version. For new projects, testify/assert is actively maintained and API-compatible.

name: github.com/smartystreets/goconvey
remediation_notes: GoConvey has been unmaintained for 3+ years despite 82K+ dependents. Its features map to testify (assertions), Ginkgo (BDD), and go test (execution). Most dependents can migrate incrementally without a 1:1 replacement.

name: github.com/jtolds/gls
remediation_notes: The author explicitly directs users to Go's standard library context package, which is the officially recommended approach. Since 95% of dependents use gls through goconvey, that project's migration would effectively resolve the ecosystem's reliance.

name: github.com/bgentry/speakeasy
remediation_notes: Tiny, stable terminal password reader with no dependencies. Copy the 186 lines into your project rather than depend on unmaintained external package.

name: github.com/hashicorp/go-uuid
remediation_notes: Migrate to google/uuid, which is actively maintained and provides RFC 4122 compliant UUID generation. With 79K+ dependents on a dormant package, switching provides better long-term support.

name: github.com/hashicorp/go-cleanhttp
remediation_notes: Zero runtime dependencies and stable, focused functionality with recent maintenance activity; pin a known version rather than forking.

name: github.com/grpc-ecosystem/go-grpc-prometheus
remediation_notes: The maintainers deprecated this in favor of go-grpc-middleware/providers/prometheus, which offers the same functionality with a modernized API. Migrate to the actively maintained replacement.

name: github.com/jmespath/go-jmespath
remediation_notes: JMESPath is a complete language spec with one primary API. Broad adoption (75k repos) across the ecosystem with no maintained alternatives means pinning a known version and accepting the dependency as-is is the only practical path.

name: github.com/google/martian/v3
remediation_notes: Archived but stable testing proxy (v3.0.0) with broad functionality—request/response modification, mocking, injection, logging. No single alternative covers it all. Pin the version; risk is low for test-only code, and Google Cloud SDK uses it fine.

name: github.com/jonboulle/clockwork
remediation_notes: Dormant but stable—no runtime dependencies, works across 75k repos. Pin the version and treat as frozen code. Alternatively, vendor the 1.4k LOC if removing the external dependency matters to your supply chain.

name: github.com/coreos/etcd
remediation_notes: The CoreOS fork is deprecated; switch to the maintained go.etcd.io/etcd module.

name: github.com/armon/go-radix
remediation_notes: Core radix tree implementation proven across 74k+ projects and stable for 7+ years with zero dependencies. Dependents should pin the version; this is not a maintenance gap but a completed utility.

name: github.com/mitchellh/go-testing-interface
remediation_notes: This archived package is complete and stable with zero runtime dependencies. Pin the version; the simple interface is unlikely to need changes.

name: github.com/posener/complete
remediation_notes: 2700 lines of stable completion logic, small enough to vendor directly. Most dependents would need architectural changes to use completion built into modern CLI frameworks, so copying the code in is the low-friction path.

name: github.com/mitchellh/cli
remediation_notes: Pinning this stable, widely-used library is low-risk; it powers Terraform and Consul. Migrate to maintained alternatives only if you expect frequent CLI changes.

name: github.com/armon/go-metrics
remediation_notes: Package explicitly deprecates in favor of hashicorp/go-metrics, maintained by HashiCorp. Update imports and verify API compatibility; most dependents should migrate cleanly.

name: github.com/hashicorp/go-immutable-radix
remediation_notes: Dormant but stable immutable radix tree with no maintained alternative. Pin to current version and accept the maintenance risk.

name: github.com/ryanuber/columnize
remediation_notes: The code is trivial (474 lines, no dependencies) and has remained stable for 5+ years without maintenance. Dependents should copy this directly into their codebase rather than maintain a separate package dependency.

name: github.com/xiang90/probing
remediation_notes: 351-line library with zero dependencies; trivial to vendor into consuming projects. Stable tool that's no longer maintained but shows no critical issues across 71k dependent repos.

name: github.com/pascaldekloe/goe
remediation_notes: Public-domain package with three independent modules, used by 71K repositories. Vendor individual modules you use or migrate to maintained alternatives (JSONPath, StatsD client, testify).

name: github.com/coreos/pkg
remediation_notes: This foundational utility collection hasn't been maintained since early 2024. Audit which utilities you actually import (logging, error handling, flags, etc.) and replace them with modern, focused alternatives—the Go ecosystem now covers all of these use cases with more specialized tools.

name: github.com/soheilhy/cmux
remediation_notes: cmux is stable, complete, and has no maintained drop-in replacement. With 71k dependents spread across the ecosystem, coordinated adoption is unrealistic. Pin versions and monitor golang.org/x/net for security updates.

name: github.com/hashicorp/logutils
remediation_notes: Stable and small (448 LOC) despite unmaintained for 8 years; 71k+ dependent repos make adoption infeasible. Pin to current version. New projects should evaluate Go's log/slog (1.21+) or structured logging packages instead.

name: github.com/tmc/grpc-websocket-proxy
remediation_notes: No maintained alternative for WebSocket-gRPC bridging exists. With 70k dependents, coordinated migration is impractical. Dormancy reflects stability; small codebase (1,009 LOC) and no dead transitive deps make pinning safe.

name: github.com/hashicorp/go-msgpack
remediation_notes: Dormant since 2018 despite 70k dependents; vmihailenco/msgpack is a maintained alternative with similar semantics.

name: github.com/subosito/gotenv
remediation_notes: Widely used (69k dependent repos) but distributed with no obvious steward. The code is mature and stable—most dependents should accept dormancy by pinning the version. Projects seeking zero dependencies can vendor the 980 LOC into their codebase.

name: github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go
remediation_notes: v1 reached end-of-support July 31, 2025. Migrate to the actively maintained v2, which provides API parity for all AWS services and official migration documentation.

name: github.com/armon/circbuf
remediation_notes: At 256 lines with no dependencies, this circular buffer implementation is small and stable enough to copy directly into consuming projects. Dependents should vendor the code to eliminate the unmaintained external dependency.

name: github.com/antihax/optional
remediation_notes: 99.4% of usage comes from grpc-gateway, which generates code depending on this optional type utility. The package is stable (616 lines, zero runtime dependencies, no security issues), so pin the version and monitor whether grpc-gateway will eventually fork or vendor it.

name: github.com/sean-/seed
remediation_notes: Copy the 10-line implementation into your code. For Go 1.20+, remove the seed call entirely—automatic seeding is now the default.

name: github.com/hashicorp/serf
remediation_notes: Serf is dormant but maintained by HashiCorp. With 68k dependents and no drop-in replacement, wholesale migration isn't feasible. Pin versions and track the armon/go-metrics deprecation (mid-2025 planned sunset).

name: github.com/hashicorp/go-syslog
remediation_notes: Zero dependencies and 7+ years without breaking changes. Major consumers (Consul, Vault, Caddy) actively maintain releases despite this package's dormancy. Pin the current version and accept the risk.

name: github.com/dustin/go-humanize
remediation_notes: Small, stable utility library with zero dependencies—unmaintained status poses minimal risk. Most dependents will accept the risk and pin versions; wholesale replacement lacks a clear drop-in alternative.

name: github.com/hashicorp/mdns
remediation_notes: Stable, feature-complete implementation of the unchanging mDNS protocol. No known security issues, clean dependencies, and active security scanning. Pin the version and monitor Go standard library compatibility.

name: github.com/niemeyer/pretty
remediation_notes: Unmaintained since 2019 with zero recent activity. go-spew is actively maintained and provides equivalent pretty-printing for Go values.

name: github.com/oklog/ulid
remediation_notes: oklog/ulid implements a stable standard with no runtime dependencies; pin the version and monitor for Go compatibility, but maintenance needs are unlikely.

name: github.com/leodido/go-urn
remediation_notes: Unmaintained for two years but implements stable RFC specs (2141, 7643, 8141) with no visible bugs. Pin to the last release and accept as a stable, read-only dependency. Fork only if RFCs change or you need patches.

name: github.com/dgryski/go-sip13
remediation_notes: Stable implementation of SipHash-2-4, a fixed cryptographic algorithm requiring no maintenance. Broadly adopted across 60k+ repos. Assembly-optimized; vendoring would sacrifice performance for no functional gain.

name: github.com/prometheus/tsdb
remediation_notes: This project was intentionally consolidated into the main Prometheus repository. Dependents should migrate to the Prometheus package directly or adopt an alternative time-series database if Prometheus doesn't fit their needs.

name: github.com/go-playground/universal-translator
remediation_notes: Unmaintained for 3+ years but feature-complete i18n library with 59k dependent repos. Pin the version; maintenance risk is minimal for stable CLDR-based pluralization and formatting code. No maintained drop-in replacement exists.

name: github.com/go-playground/locales
remediation_notes: No maintained replacement exists for full Unicode CLDR locale data in Go. Pin the version and monitor for security issues; the stable nature of locale data makes this low-risk if kept current with golang.org/x/text updates.

name: github.com/nxadm/tail
remediation_notes: Dormant for 2.5 years but zero transitive dead dependencies; tail functionality is stable and well-tested across 59k dependents. Most dependents should pin the version and monitor upstream dependencies (fsnotify, tomb.v1) for security issues rather than attempt migration.

name: github.com/mitchellh/iochan
remediation_notes: Package is trivial (67 LOC, no deps) and unmaintained for 8 years. Inlining the few hundred bytes into consuming projects eliminates dependency risk entirely.

name: github.com/hashicorp/go.net
remediation_notes: 99.7% of dependents use this indirectly through hashicorp/mdns; the package is stable despite dormancy, so pinning the version is the practical choice for most users.

name: github.com/mitchellh/gox
remediation_notes: Gox provided convenient parallelized cross-compilation before Go's toolchain matured. Replace `gox` invocations with `GOOS=<os> GOARCH=<arch> go build`. For automated release builds across platforms, consider goreleaser, but for basic cross-compilation the standard toolchain suffices.

name: github.com/armon/consul-api
remediation_notes: Deprecated in favor of the official Consul API. Dependents should migrate to `github.com/hashicorp/consul/api`, which is actively maintained by HashiCorp. The API surface is nearly identical, making this a straightforward swap.

name: github.com/xordataexchange/crypt
remediation_notes: Last commit 8 years ago; 98% of dependent usage flows through spf13/viper and its forks. The 1223-line codebase is stable and small enough to vendor directly if GPG encryption is needed, or drop entirely if using viper for standard config loading.

name: github.com/opentracing/opentracing-go
remediation_notes: OpenTracing is archived and unmaintained; OpenTelemetry is the maintained successor and CNCF standard for distributed tracing. Projects should migrate over time, though it requires updating instrumentation code beyond a simple package swap.

name: github.com/satori/go.uuid
remediation_notes: Migrate to github.com/google/uuid, actively maintained by Google with full RFC 4122 support. The API is nearly identical (NewV4 becomes New, FromString becomes Parse); migration is straightforward for most projects.

name: github.com/kr/fs
remediation_notes: Author recommends Go 1.16+ users migrate to the standard library io/fs package. For projects on older Go versions, the code is small enough to vendor if needed.

name: github.com/PuerkitoBio/purell
remediation_notes: Small, focused URL normalizer (1.5k LOC) with zero business dependencies. Easily vendorable if upstream goes dormant; copy only the flags you use.

name: github.com/PuerkitoBio/urlesc
remediation_notes: Archived since early 2024. Use Go's standard library net/url package (QueryEscape/QueryUnescape), which has matured past the RFC 3986 escaping issues this package was created to fix. Widely depended on (52k repos), but small and focused enough that switching is straightforward.

name: github.com/joho/godotenv
remediation_notes: Stable, tested, no runtime dependencies. Dormancy risk is low for code this focused. Pin the version. Alternatively, copying the 1.3K LoC inline is trivial if you want to drop the dependency.

name: github.com/go-playground/assert/v2
remediation_notes: Nearly all 51K dependents use this via go-playground/validator. That package should migrate to testify, which provides compatible assertion functions and is actively maintained. Direct users can switch independently.

name: go.uber.org/tools
remediation_notes: 98% of usage flows through go.uber.org/multierr, which is maintained. Dependents should version-pin if using directly, or rely on multierr's dependency management.

name: github.com/jessevdk/go-flags
remediation_notes: Stable utility code with no maintained drop-in replacement. Projects should pin the version and monitor for security issues.

name: github.com/pierrec/lz4
remediation_notes: klauspost/compress is actively maintained and handles LZ4 compression/decompression; switching requires refactoring to the klauspost API but is viable for most use cases and eliminates the maintenance risk of a dormant package.

name: github.com/gregjones/httpcache

name: github.com/streadway/handy

name: github.com/xanzy/ssh-agent
remediation_notes: SSH agent connectivity is stable; this 358-line package hasn't needed updates in 3+ years. Pin the version. Monitor transitive dependency security.

name: github.com/openzipkin-contrib/zipkin-go-opentracing
remediation_notes: OpenTracing is deprecated in favor of OpenTelemetry. This bridge is stable but won't receive updates; large dependents should evaluate their tracing strategy independently, as migration requires code changes in consumers.

name: github.com/containerd/fifo
remediation_notes: Dormant but stable utility for FIFO handling. Pin to the final release; this is mature library code that solves a complete problem and is unlikely to need updates.

name: github.com/googleapis/google-cloud-go-testing
remediation_notes: Archived package; README directs users to testing patterns documented in cloud.google.com/go and google.golang.org/api. The top dependent accounts for 91% of usage.

name: github.com/clbanning/x2j
remediation_notes: Explicitly deprecated 2014 in favor of mxj/x2j (same author, faster, actively maintained). Author provided x2j-wrapper subpackage for migration.

name: github.com/markbates/oncer
remediation_notes: Stable utility code with no security issues; pinning is safer than ecosystem-wide forced migration. Larger consumers can fork if needed.

name: github.com/markbates/safe
remediation_notes: Small, stable package (187 LOC) dormant since 2023 with 20k dependent repos. Dependents should vendor the code to eliminate maintenance risk rather than wait for upstream updates.

name: github.com/performancecopilot/speed
remediation_notes: 97.5% of dependents are transitive via go-kit/kit, which supports multiple metrics backends. Direct users should migrate to Prometheus unless PCP integration is required; otherwise vendor the library.

name: github.com/aryann/difflib
remediation_notes: Concentrated in go-kit/kit (99.3% of usage). If that maintained project migrates to an alternative like sergi/go-diff, nearly all downstream impact is resolved.

name: github.com/oklog/oklog
remediation_notes: Go-kit/kit accounts for 93% of dependents and should fork this package to maintain it. The code is stable but foundational. Smaller dependents can migrate logging logic to alternatives as needed.

name: github.com/containerd/go-runc
remediation_notes: Stable runc wrapper with broad ecosystem adoption. No maintained alternative exists; calling runc directly or writing custom wrappers is the only fallback. Major consumers (containerd, buildkit) actively maintained.

name: github.com/youmark/pkcs8
remediation_notes: This PKCS#8 parser is dead with 19K+ dependents scattered across the ecosystem. golang.org/x/crypto from the Go team implements the same RFC standards and receives regular security updates; this package already depends on it.

name: github.com/iancoleman/strcase
remediation_notes: Small, dependency-free string utility (596 LOC) used by 19k+ projects; copying into consuming projects is the most practical approach given the scale and simplicity.

name: github.com/DATA-DOG/go-sqlmock
remediation_notes: Complete, stable mock library with minimal dependencies and no active alternative. Safe to pin at current version.

name: github.com/garyburd/redigo
remediation_notes: Repository is archived; development moved to gomodule/redigo per the README. Switching is a drop-in replacement.

name: github.com/Masterminds/goutils
remediation_notes: Unmaintained since 2020 but widely used (19k+ repos) with no security issues. Stable string utilities; small enough (1.3k lines) to vendor if you want to drop the dependency.

name: github.com/jbenet/go-context
remediation_notes: Unmaintained for 11 years but relies only on Go's stable standard library; the breadth of dependents and lack of drop-in replacements make adoption/forking unfeasible. Pinning the version carries minimal risk.

name: github.com/Azure/go-autorest/autorest/validation
remediation_notes: Azure explicitly deprecated this package on March 31, 2023, with migration guides to azure-sdk-for-go. Validation is typically integrated into the client layer rather than a separate module in the new SDK.

name: github.com/andybalholm/cascadia
remediation_notes: Small and stable. Pin it and keep using. Goquery is available as an actively maintained alternative.

name: github.com/remyoudompheng/bigfft
remediation_notes: Stable unmaintained library for specialized FFT-based big integer multiplication. 19k dependents are mostly transitive; active users understand the trade-off. No maintenance needed for algorithmic code, but dependents should pin the version.

name: github.com/bitly/go-simplejson
remediation_notes: Three years unmaintained with no known vulnerabilities; 805 lines and zero dependencies make the risk manageable. Pin at current version and accept.

name: github.com/globalsign/mgo
remediation_notes: mgo hasn't been maintained in 7+ years. MongoDB's official driver is actively maintained and supports modern MongoDB versions (this package maxes at 3.6). Migration requires API changes but is standard practice in the Go community.

name: github.com/xdg/stringprep
remediation_notes: This package is a legacy compatibility shim; the maintainer moved to github.com/xdg-go/stringprep in 2018. Switch to the maintained fork.

name: github.com/jackc/pgpassfile
remediation_notes: Unmaintained since 2019 but stable; widely used across many small projects. Code is small enough (149 LOC) to copy into consuming projects, removing the dormant dependency entirely.

name: github.com/xdg/scram
remediation_notes: This is a deprecated legacy compatibility shim created after the package was migrated to xdg-go/scram in 2018. The author explicitly recommends switching to the maintained version as a drop-in replacement.

name: github.com/shurcooL/go
remediation_notes: Utility collection with 1703 LOC across 42 files serving 753 dependent packages (18k+ repos). Stale for 1027 days but stable and free of active issues. Pin versions and accept the maintenance risk; coordinated migration for a broad dependent base is impractical.

name: github.com/docker/libtrust
remediation_notes: Notary accounts for over half of usage, with major registry and signing tools making up the rest. The archived codebase is stable and unlikely to break; these large projects can maintain pinned versions indefinitely.

name: github.com/mrunalp/fileutils
remediation_notes: Stable file-copy utilities with no active issues—dormancy isn't a problem here. Pinning the version is safe. Dependents concerned about the dependency can inline the small codebase.

name: github.com/syndtr/goleveldb
remediation_notes: The code is stable and proven across thousands of projects. Pin your version and accept the minimal maintenance risk.

name: github.com/jackc/pgio
remediation_notes: Unchanged for 7 years with no breaking changes—safe to pin. Only 133 lines, so inlining is practical if you want to drop the dependency.

name: github.com/jackc/pgproto3/v2
remediation_notes: pgx v5 has integrated pgproto3; upgrade from pgx v4. Direct protocol users can vendor from pgx v5 or fork.

name: github.com/jackc/pgconn
remediation_notes: Archived past EOL (July 2025). Upgrade to pgx v5, which incorporates pgconn directly; major version bump requires API changes but is actively maintained.

name: github.com/jackc/chunkreader/v2
remediation_notes: Stable utility extracted from pgx with zero dependencies. No activity in 4 years reflects code maturity, not abandonment. Pin the version and treat as a stable implementation dependency.

name: github.com/jackc/pgtype
remediation_notes: pgx v5 merged pgtype's functionality into the main package; this v4-only version reached EOL July 1, 2025. Upgrade to pgx v5 to stay on a maintained codebase.

name: github.com/jackc/pgservicefile
remediation_notes: The package is only 162 lines and has been unmaintained for nearly two years. With 18k dependents scattered across the ecosystem, vendoring the minimal parser code into each project is more practical than coordinating a replacement.

name: github.com/fogleman/gg
remediation_notes: Copy the 2,800 LOC library into consuming projects. The code is self-contained with zero runtime dependencies and unlikely to need updates—dominants like go-latex should inline it rather than maintain a shared unmaintained dependency.

name: github.com/gobuffalo/genny
remediation_notes: Large projects can migrate to Go's built-in `go generate` or custom tools. Smaller dependents should evaluate whether code generation is necessary or switch to more focused alternatives.

name: github.com/jackc/puddle
remediation_notes: Puddle is feature-complete and stable with 99% of usage funneled through pgx/v4, which jackc actively maintains. Accept the dormancy; critical issues will surface through pgx. Direct users could inline the 2KB if concerned.

name: github.com/jackc/pgmock
remediation_notes: pgconn accounts for 99% of usage. Vendor the 382-line codebase into pgconn; unmaintained test infrastructure is stable and suitable for embedding.

name: github.com/jackc/pgproto3
remediation_notes: pgx v5 integrates pgproto3; migrate to it for the maintained version. Projects unable to upgrade pgx can vendor this small, self-contained codebase.

name: github.com/jackc/chunkreader
remediation_notes: Small, dependency-free I/O utility (205 LOC, 5 files) best copied into consuming projects. No commits in 4+ years; if pgproto3 inlines it, most downstream users automatically get stable code through inheritance.

name: github.com/go-logr/zapr
remediation_notes: Zapr is the standard logr-to-Zap adapter with no maintained alternative. At 1,687 lines and zero dead dependencies, it's stable to pin. The small codebase makes forking feasible if maintenance pauses.

name: github.com/gobuffalo/syncx
remediation_notes: Small utility package (520 LOC) whose largest dependents are archived Buffalo packages (packr, packd). The code can be vendored into those packages, eliminating the dependency on an unmaintained project.

name: github.com/gobuffalo/mapi
remediation_notes: Dead utility package with just 250 lines of code; dependents should vendor the codebase into their projects rather than maintain a dependency on unmaintained code.

name: github.com/jung-kurt/gofpdf
remediation_notes: Stable and feature-complete but unmaintained. Pinning the version is safe for most use cases; projects with strict maintenance policies should evaluate case-specific alternatives, as no single replacement covers all features.

name: github.com/gobuffalo/gogen
remediation_notes: This package is archived and deprecated in favor of github.com/gobuffalo/genny/gogen. The maintainers provide a clear migration path, and genny/gogen is actively maintained.

name: github.com/gobuffalo/attrs
remediation_notes: A stable utility for the gobuffalo framework inactive for 3+ years with no known issues. Dependents should pin versions and monitor whether gobuffalo itself remains maintained.

name: github.com/xlab/treeprint
remediation_notes: Stable formatting utility with no known vulnerabilities and minimal dependencies. Pin the version; low risk for a dormant library that's feature-complete.

name: github.com/gobuffalo/gitgen
remediation_notes: One dependent (gobuffalo/genny) accounts for 97% of usage; the package is archived and tiny (175 LOC). The consuming projects should inline the git utilities rather than maintaining a dead dependency.

name: github.com/docker/go-metrics
remediation_notes: Small Prometheus wrapper (773 LOC, 12 files) unmaintained for 6+ years. Trivial to inline into consuming projects; deprecation message already suggests the upgrade path (use labels instead of multiple metrics).

name: github.com/ajstarks/svgo
remediation_notes: Stable SVG generation library used across 17k+ repos with no breaking changes in 4.5 years; different consumers use different API slices, so single-alternative replacement isn't viable. Pinning the version is the practical choice.

name: github.com/boltdb/bolt
remediation_notes: Bolt is stable but archived and no longer maintained. bbolt is the actively maintained fork by the etcd project and is a drop-in replacement for most use cases.

name: github.com/agnivade/levenshtein
remediation_notes: Small, stable utility with broad adoption. Levenshtein distance is a well-defined algorithm that doesn't require active maintenance. Version pinning provides adequate protection.

name: github.com/hashicorp/yamux
remediation_notes: Yamux is stable protocol infrastructure from HashiCorp. Stream multiplexing role has no equivalent drop-in replacement; manage via pinning and security monitoring.

name: github.com/gobuffalo/depgen
remediation_notes: This package is archived and used almost entirely through genny (96.4% of dependents). Genny maintainers should vendor the small codebase (372 LoC, zero dependencies) directly.

name: github.com/shurcooL/go-goon
remediation_notes: Explicitly deprecated in favor of hexops/valast, a maintained direct replacement. Switch is low-risk because go-goon is a debugging utility, not runtime-critical.

name: github.com/getsentry/raven-go
remediation_notes: Sentry officially superseded raven-go with sentry-go and published a migration guide; most consumers can switch directly.

name: github.com/gorilla/securecookie
remediation_notes: 16,980 dependents with no clear steward; too distributed to migrate wholesale. Pin versions and monitor for vulnerabilities, contributing patches upstream if needed.

name: github.com/bugsnag/panicwrap
remediation_notes: Small, stable library with no dependencies. Last updated 4.7 years ago but functionality remains functional. Switching to the original mitchellh/panicwrap would lose the signal-handling improvements this fork adds.

name: github.com/dimchansky/utfbom
remediation_notes: At 687 lines with zero dependencies, this is straightforward to vendor. Dependents should copy the code into their project and drop the dependency, retaining full control over a stable but unattended package.

name: github.com/Azure/azure-pipeline-go
remediation_notes: Unmaintained async utilities; small enough to inline. Concentrated in Azure's own v1 SDKs, which are themselves dormant. Vendors can copy and adapt the pipeline pattern to modern Go contexts as needed.

name: github.com/certifi/gocertifi
remediation_notes: Stable CA bundle with no runtime dependencies. Last update was five years ago, but the code is immutable and correct—there's nothing to maintain. Pinning the current version is safe for all dependents.

name: github.com/Azure/azure-storage-blob-go
remediation_notes: Officially deprecated and retired as of September 2024. Azure provides a maintained replacement with a cleaner API.

name: github.com/yvasiyarov/go-metrics
remediation_notes: Unmaintained for 11+ years; prometheus/client_golang is the current Go standard for metrics collection and export. Most dependents can migrate wholesale; projects using specialized backends (Graphite, InfluxDB, Librato) may need additional exporters.

name: github.com/yvasiyarov/newrelic_platform_go
remediation_notes: SDK for New Relic's deprecated Platform API. Dependents should migrate to the maintained New Relic Go agent.

name: github.com/yvasiyarov/gorelic
remediation_notes: GoRelic is deprecated in favor of the officially maintained newrelic/go-agent. Dependents should migrate to the new package, which provides equivalent New Relic telemetry for Go with ongoing support.

name: github.com/ncw/swift
remediation_notes: Stable dormant library for OpenStack Swift. The large dependents (Vault, Thanos, Cortex) can absorb pinning this version. Swift support is legacy infrastructure code; new projects should use cloud provider SDKs directly.

name: github.com/google/shlex
remediation_notes: Shell lexing is straightforward and the codebase is small enough to vendor; most dependents should copy it in and maintain locally rather than rely on archived code.

name: github.com/bshuster-repo/logrus-logstash-hook
remediation_notes: Unmaintained for 3+ years; the minimal codebase (432 LOC, one dependency) makes vendoring practical and safer than accepting the dependency long-term.

name: github.com/bugsnag/osext
remediation_notes: Archived utility library with only 199 lines and zero dependencies. Projects should copy the code directly rather than maintain a dependency on a dead package.

name: github.com/dgryski/go-farm
remediation_notes: Go-farm is a stable hash function port with zero runtime dependencies and 15k+ verified uses. Hash algorithms don't evolve; accept dormancy and pin the version.

name: github.com/golangci/lint-1
remediation_notes: golint is archived; golangci-lint is the actively maintained Go linter that superseded it. It's compatible with golint-style checks and is now the community standard.

name: github.com/mattn/go-ieproxy
remediation_notes: Thin wrapper around Windows and macOS system APIs for proxy detection. No active maintenance since 706 days, but unlikely to break without major OS changes. Azure ecosystem (88.6% of usage) should establish a maintenance plan or fork.

name: github.com/Shopify/logrus-bugsnag
remediation_notes: Stable integration that doesn't require active maintenance. Pin the version; the code has proven mature. Projects seeking to change error reporters should do so independently based on their needs.

name: github.com/mistifyio/go-zfs
remediation_notes: ZFS wrapper with stable underlying tools, no transitive vulnerabilities, feature-complete. Dependents should pin version explicitly and monitor for ZFS protocol changes.

name: github.com/marstr/guid
remediation_notes: Unmaintained for 5+ years; google/uuid is the standard maintained Go library for RFC 4122 UUIDs and is a drop-in replacement for most use cases. Large projects like Kubernetes likely pinned to a known version, but new adoption should target google/uuid.

name: github.com/mgutz/ansi
remediation_notes: This 545-line ANSI color library is stable but unmaintained. Fatih/color is the maintained standard that most projects should switch to. Smaller consumer projects could alternatively vendor this trivial code, but switching is cleaner for the ecosystem.

name: github.com/kballard/go-shellquote
remediation_notes: Stable unmaintained utility with 15K+ dependents. No maintained alternative; keep pinned and monitor for vulnerabilities only.

name: github.com/jinzhu/gorm
remediation_notes: GORM V1 is dormant; the official upgrade is GORM V2 (github.com/go-gorm/gorm), actively maintained with a straightforward migration path.

name: github.com/denverdino/aliyungo
remediation_notes: This archived SDK is superseded by Aliyun's official SDK, which the original maintainer references in the README. Dependents should migrate to the maintained version.

name: github.com/gorilla/sessions
remediation_notes: This is a stable, small codebase (1020 LOC) safe to vendor into consuming projects. No maintained drop-in replacement exists; projects on older Go versions are already pinned to v1.3.0 anyway, making vendoring the practical next step.

name: github.com/shurcooL/httpfs
remediation_notes: Small stable library (785 LOC) with no runtime dependencies providing http.FileSystem utilities. 92.6% of usage flows through gopherjslib, also unmaintained. Straightforward to vendor needed functionality inline.

name: github.com/microcosm-cc/bluemonday
remediation_notes: Bluemonday is a mature, proven HTML sanitizer with 15k dependents. While dormant, it's stable for XSS prevention. Forking saddles you with security code maintenance; switching requires multiple tools. Pin the version and monitor the two published advisories.

name: github.com/twitchyliquid64/golang-asm
remediation_notes: Unmaintained since 2020 but stable—it mirrors Go's internal assembler. 6,400+ dependents across many projects means no single steward will emerge. Pin the version and accept the maintenance risk; vendoring 58k LOC is impractical at scale.

name: github.com/cockroachdb/logtags
remediation_notes: Dormant maintenance (last commit 500 days ago, last release 1196 days ago) but the implementation is stable, simple, and self-contained—copy the ~300 lines of code into your project to eliminate dependency risk for this narrow-purpose utility.

name: github.com/Azure/go-autorest/autorest/azure/cli
remediation_notes: Azure officially retired support on March 31, 2023 and provides migration guides. Goreleaser (46% of usage) and Azure service dependents should migrate to the maintained azure-sdk-for-go family.

name: github.com/Masterminds/sprig
remediation_notes: Sprig is a stable library with 100+ template functions and no maintained alternative. Protoc-gen-doc drives 73% of usage; other dependents should pin versions and accept dormancy risk rather than fork, vendor, or switch.

name: github.com/lyft/protoc-gen-star
remediation_notes: Dormant but stable plugin framework with no dead transitive dependencies. Dependents should migrate to protoc-gen-go, buf, or custom implementations; refactoring burden varies by plugin complexity.

name: gopkg.in/mgo.v2
remediation_notes: Unmaintained for 7 years; globalsign/mgo is a community-maintained drop-in fork recommended by the original author.

name: github.com/otiai10/mint
remediation_notes: Three-year-old unmaintained test assertion library. testify/assert is the maintained standard with nearly identical API; migration is straightforward.

name: github.com/otiai10/curr
remediation_notes: A 139-line wrapper around Go's runtime package with zero external dependencies. Most dependents use only some of the seven entry points; feasible and recommended to vendor the needed code directly into each project.

name: github.com/matryer/is
remediation_notes: Dormant assertion library with 14K dependents across many projects. testify/assert is actively maintained with an equivalent API and broader coverage, suitable for wholesale migration.

name: github.com/Azure/go-autorest/autorest/azure/auth
remediation_notes: Azure deprecated go-autorest on 2023-03-31. Use the active azure-sdk-for-go replacement; migration guides available for authentication (azidentity) and other modules.

name: github.com/gobwas/ws
remediation_notes: go-micro drives ~48% of usage; gorilla/websocket and nhooyr/websocket are actively maintained drop-in replacements. Heavy users should lead migration.

name: github.com/gobwas/pool
remediation_notes: Unmaintained for 7 years but small and stable. Dependents should migrate to Go's sync.Pool or vendor the code.

name: github.com/gobwas/httphead
remediation_notes: Unmaintained since ~April 2021 but stable and dependency-free. Small enough to vendor safely; fragmented dependents should each copy it in to future-proof against upstream rot.

name: github.com/otiai10/copy
remediation_notes: A stable utility with 13k dependent repos and no obvious steward. At 1,815 lines focused on recursive directory copying, it's small enough to vendor directly rather than wait for maintenance. Most projects can inline the core logic or copy the code and pin it.

name: github.com/mohae/deepcopy
remediation_notes: At 1,111 lines with zero runtime dependencies, this stable deep-copy implementation is small enough for dependents to vendor directly into their codebases. This eliminates the external dependency risk from unmaintained code while preserving all existing APIs.

name: github.com/coreos/go-iptables
remediation_notes: Dormant but stable zero-dependency iptables wrapper with 91% of usage in containernetworking/plugins. Small enough and simple enough to safely vendor; copying the code eliminates all external dependency risk.

name: github.com/chenzhuoyu/base64x
remediation_notes: Switch to the standard library's encoding/base64 (built-in, no external dependency). Main tradeoff is performance—base64x exists because stdlib was slow, but modern Go has caught up and the maintenance risk may exceed the performance benefit.

name: github.com/mitchellh/osext
remediation_notes: osext provides utilities for finding the executable path/directory—functionality Go stdlib's os.Executable() (available since 1.8) covers. Unmaintained but stable; projects should migrate to stdlib equivalents. Pinning is safe for legacy code.

name: github.com/mattn/goveralls
remediation_notes: For GitHub Actions workflows, switch to shogo82148/actions-goveralls. For direct CLI use, the codebase is stable and small enough to vendor, or pin the version.

name: github.com/tidwall/gjson
remediation_notes: GJSON is unmaintained with 4 unpatched advisories. The codebase is small and stable enough to copy into consuming projects; distributed vendoring is more practical than waiting for upstream fixes or forking at scale.

name: github.com/k0kubun/colorstring
remediation_notes: Unmaintained for 11 years but stable. Copy the 242 lines of color-parsing code into your project to drop the dependency entirely.

name: github.com/logrusorgru/aurora
remediation_notes: Aurora is dormant with no active maintenance, but remains stable with zero security issues. Maintained alternatives like fatih/color provide equivalent ANSI color functionality and are widely used.

name: github.com/d2g/dhcp4
remediation_notes: Kubernetes ecosystem accounts for 60%+ of usage; others mostly depend transitively. Switch to insomniacslk/dhcp for active maintenance and modern DHCP support.
